A symptom-permissive output contract closed the reversal's breadth end but not its ordering end, and blinded physicians judged neither strategy's errors more dangerous (68% ties; a null powered for large effects only). Interpretation. Multi-agent pipelines are input-conditional: they improve differential-list recall (not top-1 accuracy) on curated inputs and underperform on uncurated emergency text - a label-level reversal without a clinician-judged safety difference. Strategy selection should key on the input and model family, observable before the model runs, as a routing hypothesis; curated-benchmark gains should not be extrapolated to front-line care.

items.title_en: MULTIMODAL EEG WORLD MODEL: SELF-SUPERVISED LATENT TRANSITION LEARNING FOR WEARABLE EEG SEIZURE DETECTION
items.abstract_en: Existing supervised and self-supervised EEG models mainly learn within-segment discriminative or reconstructive representations, leaving transitions between adjacent EEG segments underexplored. We propose a self-supervised Multimodal EEG World Model for EEG seizure detection that predicts the latent representation of the next EEG segment from the current EEG state, conditioned on synchronized ECG, EMG, and movement signals. A learnable query-based fusion module aggregates the multimodal synchronized signals into a compact physiological condition. Pretraining uses no seizure labels; downstream detection retains only the frozen EEG encoder and a linear probe. On the SeizeIT2 dataset with a strict patient-wise split, the model achieved an AUPRC of 0.3748, ROC-AUC of 0.8025, and balanced accuracy of 0.7308, outperforming official database baselines (SVM with hand-crafted features and ChronoNet), an external baseline (DSAINet), and a foundation model (NeuroLM). Ablations show a 14.4% relative AUPRC gain over a random-initialized encoder, supporting multimodal-conditioned latent transition learning for wearable EEG representation learning.

items.title_en: Seeded Probes Do Not Identify a Reviewer's Miss Rate: One-Sided Misclassification in Distribution-Free Risk Control
items.abstract_en: Distribution-free risk control certifies that the rate of defects that would change clinical management, among the answers an AI system releases, stays below a stated level, calibrated on cases a human reviewer has checked. The reviewer is an imperfect reference standard whose errors run one way: a missed defect enters calibration as a safe label. This one-sided misclassification lowers the risk on record at every release threshold, so the certificate is anti-conservative by a factor set by the reviewer's miss rate on the system's own defects. We show that seeded probes, which plant known defects and count the catches, do not identify this miss rate. A reviewer's chance of missing a defect depends on how hard that defect is to spot, its detectability. A probe samples defects at detectabilities its designer chose. The system's own defects fall at detectabilities nothing chose, and converting the probe's miss rate into theirs requires the very rate being sought. This holds whenever detectability is not fully captured by an observed score, since a score that captured it would let probes covering its range identify the rate. Cytology field validation builds probe sets whose miss rate is a floor on the true one. Even then the probe bounds the rate from below only, so it can reject a certificate and cannot grant one. The finite-sample label-noise corrections assume noise independent of the case given its label, but a reviewer misses the defects that read as plausible, and the condition they need fails in all four simulated reviewer profiles we examine. Testing that condition on an independent sample takes 185 adjudicated cases for a reviewer missing 85% of defects and 147,938 for one missing 3%. A second reader who adjudicates the cases the careful reviewer passed finds a miss with 95% confidence within 498, so looking for the noise directly costs far less than testing a model of it. In a public corpus of model answers graded by physicians, a physician passed 26.3% of the defects the other graders agreed were there (95% interval 21.6% to 31.7%, resampling whole conversations), on criteria about seeking context and stating uncertainty, and individual rates ran from 8.0% to 54.5%.

items.title_en: Association of neurotransmitter-based polygenic scores with antidepressant treatment outcomes in patients with major depressive disorder
items.abstract_en: Biologically informed polygenic scores (PGSs) may help interpret genetic associations with treatment outcomes. Here, we computed neurotransmitter-based PGSs (NeuroPGSs) for patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) and assessed their association with SSRI treatment outcomes. By targeting genetic variants involved in key neurotransmission pathways, we developed PGSs for serotonergic (5228), gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA, 4103), dopaminergic (7061), and glutamatergic (5690) variants. We leveraged data from two cohorts of patients who received SSRIs for at least 4 weeks: the International SSRI Pharmacogenomics Consortium (ISPC) and the Pharmacogenomics Research Network Antidepressants Medication Pharmacogenomics Study (PGRN-AMPS). Treatment response was defined as [≥]50% reduction from baseline depression symptoms, measured using 17-item Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD-17) in ISPC and 16-item Quick Inventory of Depressive Symptomatology (QIDS-C16) in PGRN-AMPS. Remission was defined as HRSD-17 [≤]7 (ISPC) or QIDS-C16[≤]5 (PGRN-AMPS). The association between each NeuroPGS and antidepressant response or remission was evaluated using logistic regression models, adjusting for age, sex and five genetic principal components, with statistical significance determined at Benjamini Hochberg-adjusted p<0.05. The GABAergic-based PGS was associated with SSRI response (aOR per SD = 1.45, 95%CI: 1.14-1.85). Patients with the highest GABAergic PGS (10th decile) had 2.59-fold higher odds of response (95%CI: 1.46-4.60) compared to those with the lowest decile (1st decile). These exploratory findings support further evaluation of NeuroPGSs; independent replication and assessment of incremental predictive value are needed before clinical application. Keywords: Polygenic score; Neurotransmitters; GABAergic; depression; SSRIs; pharmacogenomics

items.title_en: Outcome definition and index validity in cross-national comparisons of diet-attributable metabolic burden
items.abstract_en: Background: In three national surveys, no cross-national ranking of diet-attributable metabolic burden was identified: the apparent ordering moved with the definition of the outcome and with the validity of the dietary index. Both were tested. Subjects/Methods: We harmonised individual-participant data from national surveys in the USA (NHANES 2017-2018), Korea (KNHANES 2015-2021) and Mexico (ENSANUT 2018-2019); 56,365 adults in total, recovered Mexican blood-pressure data from the raw files, and defined metabolic syndrome (MetS) with a common five-component ATP III rule. We estimated survey-weighted sex-specific associations of the energy-adjusted Dietary Inflammatory Index (E-DII) with MetS, country-specific population-attributable fractions (PAFs) on a common counterfactual scale, and the E-DII correlation with log high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP). A quantitative bias analysis examined whether validity differences could reverse the country ordering. Results: The E-DII-MetS association was larger in women (USA OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.98-1.55; Korea 1.078, 1.028-1.132; Mexico 1.074, 0.992-1.163; interaction P=0.080) but disappeared without blood pressure in the outcome (pooled 1.065, 0.982-1.155; P=0.13). Female PAFs were 15.0%, 7.6% and 3.8%; no pairwise difference was distinguishable (all P>=0.23). E-DII validity was 0.137 in US women versus 0.040 in Korean women (P=2.0x10-4); the validity ratio was 0.29, correction reversed the observed ordering, and its interval straddled the reversal threshold. Conclusions: Neither the direction nor the magnitude of cross-national differences in diet-attributable MetS burden was identified; the ordering was bounded by outcome definition and by index validity. Cross-national burden comparisons require local validation of both.

items.title_en: FreqFuseNet: Scale-Normalized Dual-Frequency Fusion for Thin-Wall Head-and-Neck OAR Segmentation
items.abstract_en: Accurate segmentation of thin-wall organs-at-risk (OARs) in head-and-neck computed tomography (CT) is challenging because small contour deviations can substantially affect boundary agreement. We present FreqFuseNet, a segmentation architecture with a fast Fourier transform (FFT) primary branch and a frequency channel attention network (FcaNet) residual branch that explicitly aligns heterogeneous frequency-feature scales before bounded residual fusion. An initialization-time analysis revealed an approximately 863-fold activation-scale disparity between the two branches, corresponding to an approximately 43-fold unintended residual-to-primary magnitude ratio under naive fusion with a nominal coefficient of 0.05. FreqFuseNet uses per-sample, per-channel scale alignment to preserve the intended relative amplitude without additional normalization parameters. We evaluated 10 thin-wall OARs on SegRap2023 (84 training, 18 validation, and 18 testing CT cases) under a standardized binary per-OAR region-of-interest (ROI) protocol. In two training seeds, FreqFuseNet achieved Dice of 0.849 and 0.843, 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 0.824 and 0.823 mm, and surface Dice at 1 mm of 0.959 and 0.957. In case-level paired comparisons for the primary seed (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, not corrected for multiple comparisons), FreqFuseNet showed significant improvements over 3D U-Net and MedNeXt-S, whereas differences versus an alternative learned fusion design (FixedFusion) and SegResNet were not statistically significant. These findings identify a practical feature-scale calibration issue in dual-frequency segmentation and demonstrate competitive boundary-sensitive performance of the proposed architecture within the evaluated ROI-based setting.

items.title_en: Improving Survival Prediction from Surrogate Endpoints Through Integration of Patient-Reported Outcomes Using Machine Learning
items.title_zh: 利用机器学习整合患者报告结局以改进基于替代终点的生存预测
items.abstract_en: Introduction: Overall survival (OS) is the gold standard for demonstrating treatment benefit in oncology but requires prolonged follow-up. Surrogate efficacy endpoints, such as progression-free survival, can shorten trial duration and reduce costs but may not consistently reflect overall survival benefit. We hypothesized that integrating patient-reported outcomes (PROs) with surrogate endpoints would improve trial-level prediction of OS benefit. Methods: We reviewed clinical trials supporting FDA oncology drug approvals from 2013 to 2023 that reported OS, at least one surrogate efficacy endpoint, and PROs. Machine learning models predicted OS benefit were developed using surrogate endpoints alone or surrogate endpoint features combined with PROs. Both models were validated using repeated five-fold trial-grouped cross-validation and leave-one-trial-out validation. Results: A total of 100 clinical trials (103 between-arm comparisons, 68,987 participants) met inclusion criteria. Compared with control arms, 68% of active treatment arms demonstrated OS benefit, 83.5% showed surrogate endpoints improvement, and 35.9% showed improvement in PROs. Adding PROs to machine learning models increased area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) from 0.67 (95% CI, 0.55- 0.78) to 0.79 (95% CI, 0.69- 0.87), an absolute increase of 0.12 indicating improved model discrimination. Leave-one-trial-out validation confirmed the improvement (AUC-ROC, 0.663 versus 0.795; paired difference, 0.132; 95% CI, 0.017- 0.248). Conclusions: Integrating PROs with surrogate endpoints improved prediction of OS benefit, supporting machine learning as a quantitative framework for combining complementary endpoints in oncology drug development.

items.title_en: Spatially Informed and Direction Sensitive Representation Learning for Spatial Transcriptomics
items.title_zh: 面向空间转录组学的空间信息感知与方向敏感表征学习
items.abstract_en: Cellular states are shaped by both intrinsic gene expression programs and the spatial microenvironment in which cells reside. Spatial transcriptomics makes this context measurable, but effective representation learning requires capturing both spatially informative molecular signals and intercellular organization. Existing approaches address these challenges only partially: conventional gene selection can overlook spatially structured signals, while methods for encoding cell-cell relationships often either reduce a cell's microenvironment to proximity alone, discarding direction, or rely on absolute coordinates tied to an arbitrary tissue frame. Consequently, cells with similar neighbor distances but distinct spatial organization may receive overly similar representations, despite experiencing different biological contexts that shape their cellular states. We introduce Tessera, a spatial representation learning framework that addresses both molecular selection and cellular context. Tessera combines spatially informed gene selection with a geometric inductive bias that contextualizes each cell within its local tissue environment. By modeling relative cell-cell relationships, Tessera is translation-invariant while preserving direction, allowing neighboring cells to contribute differently according to their spatial context and cellular state. Across held-out tissues and technologies, Tessera outperforms existing spatial foundation models in representation quality and generalizes zero-shot to contexts up to $16\times$ larger than those seen during training.
items.abstract_zh: 细胞状态由内在基因表达程序与所处空间微环境共同塑造，空间转录组学使这一背景可测量，但有效表征学习需同时捕获具空间信息的分子信号与细胞间组织方式。现有方法只能部分应对：传统基因选择可能忽略空间结构信号；编码细胞关系的方法或仅以邻近性概括微环境而丢失方向，或依赖组织坐标系中的绝对位置。于是邻近距离相似但空间组织不同的细胞可能得到过于相似的表示。作者提出 Tessera，将空间信息驱动的基因选择与几何归纳偏置结合，把每个细胞置于其局部组织环境中刻画；通过建模相对细胞关系实现平移不变的同时保留方向，使邻居按空间上下文与细胞状态贡献不同。在留出组织与不同技术平台上，Tessera 的表示质量优于现有空间基础模型，并可零样本泛化到训练时16倍大的上下文。
items.highlight_zh: Tessera：保留方向信息的相对关系建模，提升空间转录组表征
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：空间转录组能同时测到每个细胞表达了哪些基因、以及它在组织中的位置。要让机器学习利用这类数据，需要把细胞编码成向量，而这个向量既要反映基因程序，也要反映它所处的组织处境。现有做法有两处短板：挑基因时可能漏掉有空间格局的信号；描述邻居关系时，要么只算距离（丢掉方向），要么用组织切片的绝对坐标（换个取样位置就失效）。
方法：作者提出 Tessera。第一，基因选择考虑空间信息，优先保留在组织中有空间结构的基因；第二，用几何归纳偏置建模“相对”的细胞间关系——用邻居相对于自己的方向与状态来刻画微环境，于是表示对整体平移不变，却保留方向性，不同方向、不同状态的邻居贡献不同。
结果：在未见过的组织和多种技术平台上，Tessera 的表示质量优于现有空间基础模型；还能零样本迁移到比训练时大16倍的空间上下文范围。
为何重要：这意味着模型不必为每个新切片重新训练，就能捕获“组织架构”这一层生物学信息，对区分空间位置不同但表达相近的细胞状态，以及跨样本、跨平台分析都有实际价值。

items.title_en: An Open Reliability Atlas of Sensitivity and Failure Modes in the Pulse Physiology Engine
items.abstract_en: Pulse is an actively maintained open-source adult-physiology simulator, yet its maintainers report no formal sensitivity analysis of its operational inputs. We present the first open reliability atlas across its critical-care envelope: Morris elementary-effects sampling of seven inputs, four severity scenarios, male and female bodies (1,280 simulations). Sensitivity is skewed: three inputs carry a median 93% of each output's total. A four-flag classifier reveals failure modes: two operator-actionable, one sex-stratified. Tidal-volume oscillation (20.6% of runs) is consistent with patient-ventilator dyssynchrony; locking the VC-AC trigger to -2 cmH2O collapses that variability. At FiO2 = 1.0, transient hyperoxia makes 120-second runs underestimate plateau PaO2; 300-second healthy-lung reruns give a median 643 mmHg. Solver divergence was all-male in an input-extreme regime (20/1,280); reducing the male blood-volume baseline to the 4,082 mL floor eliminated it. Runs and flags are released openly, showing users which regions need checking before training on Pulse output.

items.title_en: What I Disbelieve: Quantifying Belief With Negative Ranking Functions
items.abstract_en: A challenge in exploring the psychology of human uncertainty is its measurement and quantification. Prior work has focused almost exclusively on probability, while the formal theories developed in philosophy are rarely tested. We tested Wolfgang Spohn's ranking theory, a normative account in which belief is graded by ordinal ranks of disbelief that combine by minimization rather than addition, as a descriptive model of human belief. Across six experiments, participants assigned ranks of disbelief to propositions involving personal experience, chance devices, sequential learning, and an Ellsberg urn. Ranks were reliable and, through the theory's two-sided rank function, distinguished belief, disbelief, and suspension of judgment. Participants respected the Law of Negation, never disbelieving both a proposition and its complement, in every task except a lottery. Disjunctions did not follow the theory's Law of Disjunction. Instead of taking the minimum rank of the disjuncts, participants averaged them. In a learning task, ranks aligned more closely than did subjective probabilities with objective probabilities. In an Ellsberg Urn scenario, the paradoxical behavior seen with betting was markedly reduced by ranks. We conclude that human belief has the bipolar, negation-respecting structure that ranking theory proposes, but combines disjuncts by averaging rather than by minimization. As a clear account of human belief dynamics with metrics that can be reliably measured, Ranking Theory provides a valuable framework for investigating and contrasting probabilistic and non-probabilistic accounts of human belief.

items.title_en: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
items.title_zh: GBClaw：面向原子尺度晶界研究与机理发现的智能体 AI 框架
items.abstract_en: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.
items.abstract_zh: 智能体 AI 系统在自动化材料发现流程上潜力巨大，但扩展到需要深厚领域知识的机理研究仍具挑战。本文提出 GBClaw，用于研究一般晶界的结构与变形。一般晶界占多晶材料实际界面的绝大多数，却因结构复杂、界面失配而研究不足。GBClaw 把大语言模型集成到由编排器、专用智能体、领域工具、模拟接口与分层记忆构成的模块化架构中，通过动态重规划与迭代工作流优化，将系统性模拟与针对性机理分析连接起来。应用于镍中14个一般非对称倾转晶界，GBClaw 表征了界面缺陷结构并识别出多种变形模式；对比有无次级晶界失配位错的滑移，发现剪切强度差异显著，凸显缺陷层级对滑移阻力的关键作用；研究者引导的后续计算还将异常高的剪切阻力追溯到亚稳界面结构。
items.highlight_zh: 智能体 AI 自动完成镍晶界模拟与机理分析，揭示缺陷层级控制滑移阻力
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：多晶材料中的界面绝大多数是“一般晶界”——取向差任意、结构杂乱。这类晶界恰恰难以实验表征，也难以用常规计算逐个遍查，因此长期被研究得最少，却又主导着材料的强度与变形行为。
方法：作者构建了 GBClaw，一个智能体式 AI 框架。它以大型语言模型为核心，配有编排器、若干专职子智能体、领域工具与模拟接口，以及分层记忆；它能自行规划任务、调用原子尺度模拟、依据中间结果动态重规划，把大批量模拟与针对性的机理分析串联起来。
结果：在镍的14个一般非对称倾转晶界上运行，GBClaw 系统刻画了界面缺陷结构，识别出多种不同的变形模式；通过对比有无次级晶界失配位错时的滑移，发现剪切强度差别显著，说明缺陷的层级结构对滑移阻力至关重要；在研究者引导的后续计算中，还把一处异常高的剪切阻力追溯到亚稳的界面结构。
为何重要：它示范了智能体 AI 与领域知识如何把高通量计算筛选和深层物理理解接上，让原本因复杂而“算不动”的一般晶界变得可系统研究，为界面工程与材料设计提供新范式。

items.title_en: Characterizing supersolid phase transitions in trapped quantum gases with tilted dipoles at finite temperature
items.title_zh: 有限温度下倾斜偶极囚禁量子气体中超固态相变的表征
items.abstract_en: Motivated by a recent experimental work $[\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20327}{\text{arXiv:}2608.20327}]$, we theoretically investigate the nature of phase transitions in a trapped dipolar quantum gas upon tuning the contact interaction strength and dipole orientation. Using extended Gross-Pitaevskii simulations including thermal and quantum effects, we map the phase diagram comprising unmodulated superfluids, triangular droplet arrays, and stripe states. We further characterize the order of the transitions separating them through imaginary-time hysteresis analysis. The unmodulated-to-modulated transition evolves from discontinuous to continuous with increasing dipole tilt before becoming discontinuous again at large tilts. The degree of continuity is further affected by particle number, temperature, and confinement. While continuous behavior generally correlates with the emergence of stripe states, this correspondence is not systematic, and finite-size effects also influence the continuity of the transition. The triangular-to-stripe transition is found to be discontinuous at small contact interaction strengths and becomes increasingly continuous upon approaching the unmodulated-to-modulated phase boundary. Our results reveal a tunable transition order in finite dipolar quantum gases and provide guidance for its experimental investigation.
items.abstract_zh: 受近期实验工作启发，本文理论研究囚禁偶极量子气体在调节接触相互作用强度和偶极取向时相变的性质。作者采用包含热效应与量子效应的扩展 Gross-Pitaevskii 模拟，绘制出由无调制超流体、三角液滴阵列和条纹态构成的相图，并通过虚时滞回分析判定相变阶数。随偶极倾角增大，无调制—有调制相变由不连续转为连续，在大倾角下又变为不连续；连续性程度还受粒子数、温度和束缚条件影响。连续行为通常与条纹态的出现相关，但这种对应并不系统，有限尺寸效应也会影响相变的连续性。三角—条纹相变在小接触相互作用强度下不连续，接近无调制—有调制相界时逐渐变为连续。结果揭示了有限偶极量子气体中可调的相变阶数，并为实验研究提供指引。
items.highlight_zh: 偶极量子气体超固态相变的阶数可由倾角、温度与相互作用调节
items.digest_zh:
研究问题：偶极量子气体（原子间具有长程各向异性相互作用）在特定条件下会形成“超固态”——既具备超流般的相位相干性，又呈现类似晶体的密度调制。实验上通过调节接触相互作用和偶极取向（倾角）来驱动这类相变，但相变究竟是“突变”还是“渐变”、由什么控制，此前缺乏系统的理论刻画。
方法：作者用包含热效应与量子涨落的扩展 Gross-Pitaevskii 方程模拟囚禁的偶极气体，扫描接触相互作用强度与偶极倾角，画出包含无调制超流体、三角液滴阵列和条纹态的相图；再用虚时滞回分析判断相变阶数（不连续还是连续）。
结果：1）无调制到有调制的相变随倾角增大由不连续变连续，倾角很大时又回到不连续；粒子数、温度和束缚强度也会改变连续性程度。2）连续相变通常伴随条纹态出现，但两者并非一一对应，有限尺寸效应也参与其中。3）三角到条纹的相变在小接触相互作用下不连续，越靠近无调制—有调制相界越趋于连续。
为何重要：这说明有限尺寸偶极气体中的相变阶数是可以“调”的，为解读和设计相关实验（例如如何判断是否为真正的连续相变）提供了具体指引。

items.title_en: Cumulative locality governs collective quantum charging
items.title_zh: 累积局域性主导集体量子充电
items.abstract_en: Quantum batteries can outperform their classical counterparts through collective quantum effects, yet the conditions enabling such advantage remain unclear. Using a generic class of free-fermionic chargers we prove that global operators are insufficient for scalable superextensive charging and that a cumulative hierarchy of many-body operators is required, with the structure of the battery determining the degree of advantage. This is obtained by relating the charging power to the norm of the commutator between the battery and charger Hamiltonians and deriving an upper bound only capturing noncommuting terms. Moreover, we revisit the concept of participation number and propose an effective definition that accounts for the relative strength of the contributing terms, correlating it with the charging power scaling. Not limited to quadratic Hamiltonians, our results establish cumulative locality as a key resource for quantum charging advantage.
items.abstract_zh: 量子电池可通过集体量子效应超越经典电池，但实现这种优势所需的条件仍不清楚。我们针对一类通用的自由费米子充电器证明：仅靠全局算符无法实现可扩展的超广延充电，必须依赖多体算符构成的累积层级结构，而电池自身的结构决定优势的大小。该结论的得出，依赖于将充电功率与电池和充电器哈密顿量之间对易子的范数关联起来，并推导出一个只涵盖非对易项的上界。此外，我们重新审视参与数的概念，提出一种考虑各贡献项相对强度的有效定义，并将其与充电功率的标度行为相联系。我们的结果并不局限于二次哈密顿量，从而确立了累积局域性作为量子充电优势的关键资源。
items.highlight_zh: 累积局域性是量子电池超广延充电优势的关键资源
items.digest_zh:
【研究问题】量子电池利用集体量子效应，理论上可以比经典电池充得更快，但究竟什么样的电池结构、什么样的充电源才能让这种优势随电池规模持续放大，此前缺乏明确的判据。
【方法思路】作者从一类通用的自由费米子充电器出发，把充电功率与「电池哈密顿量和充电器哈密顿量之间的对易子范数」挂钩，进而推导出一个只由非对易项决定的上界。这一数学处理把「谁能提供有效充电」转化为「哈密顿量中哪些多体项彼此不对易」。
【主要结果】结论有两点：单靠全局（整体性）算符无法随规模扩展出超广延的充电功率；需要的是多体算符按某种「累积层级」逐级叠加，而电池的具体结构决定最终能获得多大优势。作者还指出，传统的「参与数」指标会误导判断，因此提出考虑各贡献项相对强度的新定义，发现它与充电功率的标度关系吻合。
【为何重要】这项工作给出了设计量子电池的定量指导：不是简单地增加纠缠或使用全局耦合，而是要精心构造具有累积局域性的多体相互作用。它还提供了可检验的上界与指标，且不限于二次型哈密顿量，为后续实验与材料层面的实现提供了理论标尺。

items.title_en: Complete Modified Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for one-dimensional quantum Spin Chain
items.title_zh: 一维量子自旋链的完全修正对数Sobolev不等式
items.abstract_en: We prove a complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality with a system-size-independent constant for Chen--Kastoryano--Gilyén Gibbs samplers on one-dimensional spin chain at every fixed positive temperature. The result holds for Hamiltonians with bounded finite-range interactions, including noncommuting and spatially nonuniform interactions. It yields trace and diamond mixing times of order $O(\log N+\log(1/ε))$. The proof establishes complete spatial entropy factorization and absorbs quasi-local errors as conditional relative entropy at the original joint state and reference. The static estimate also yields a system-size-independent CMLSI for the single-site Petz heat-bath and regularised heat-bath dynamics.

items.title_en: Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Switch Networks: Memory Limits and Achievability
items.title_zh: 量子开关网络中的纠缠分发：内存限制与可达性
items.abstract_en: We study the minimum persistent memory required to distribute a graph state through a quantum switch. Specifically, consider a central switch that assists $n$ remote users in distributing a graph state, using independently generated user-switch Bell pairs. Since Bell-pair generation is probabilistic, different links generally succeed at different times. When a Bell-pair is generated, the qubits may need to be stored in memory while waiting for other links to succeed. Recently, new protocols have been proposed to reduce this storage overhead by processing and releasing some switch qubits before all Bell links are available. However, these protocols do not characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required at each stage. Moreover, the local-cover method in the state-of-the-art Piecemaker protocol is computationally expensive for general target graphs. In this work, we characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required after any subset of users' Bell links are generated and processed. We then develop an online stabilizer-transition protocol that attains this limit, which can be implemented in polynomial time in the number of qubits $n$. Remarkably, this optimal protocol can provide substantial memory reductions over existing heuristic approaches. In particular, for the path graph $P_n$ over $n$ users, Piecemaker protocol requires at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ qubits of peak persistent memory for \textit{every Bell-links generation order}, whereas under the order $(1,2,\ldots,n)$, our protocol requires only one persistent switch qubit. Finally, the same stabilizer-transition framework also provides a direct forward construction for sequential graph-state generation using the minimum number of quantum emitters, equal to the maximum of the height function.

items.title_en: Correcting topographic artifacts in three-dimensional ToF-SIMS: A practical guide from data-only reconstruction to correlative AFM
items.title_zh: 校正三维ToF-SIMS中的形貌伪影：从纯数据重建到关联AFM的实用指南
items.abstract_en: Three-dimensional time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (3D ToF-SIMS) builds chemical volumes by stacking images acquired between sputter cycles. Standard reconstruction assumes a flat starting surface and a single sputter rate, so samples with topography, or with layers that sputter at different rates, yield distorted interface positions and depth scales. This article is a practical guide to correcting these artifacts. We group the available corrections by the information they need: the SIMS data alone, atomic force microscopy (AFM) topography before and after the profile, or AFM topography also at intermediate stages. All three are applied to a model Pt/TaOx/Ta/Pt/Ti crossbar memristor device measured with in situ SIMS/AFM at ten stages, together with the data preparation they share. Each correction method is evaluated using the known device geometry and the measured surface evolution. The data-only correction requires no additional instrumentation and restores relative topography, but its depth scale depends on nominal layer thicknesses and remains unconstrained below the last calibrated interface. AFM before and after the profile fixes the start and end surfaces but assumes uniform sputtering in between, which fails next to the device, where the surroundings change material during the profile. Multi-stage AFM correction follows these changes and reproduces the structure of the device, at the cost of instrument time and repeated imaging of a partially sputtered surface. A decision flowchart and a checklist help readers choose, validate and report a correction.

items.title_en: NeST: ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes with sub-$50μ$s stabiliser cycles via spin shuttling
items.title_zh: NeST：通过自旋穿梭实现稳定子循环低于50μs的超高速率qLDPC码
items.abstract_en: Quantum low-density parity-check codes now reach encoding rates up to 50% at useful distances. Their checks however are long-range group actions, not local neighbourhoods, and that connectivity has so far been supplied by neutral atoms. Silicon spin qubits offer the same primitive --- coherent transport of qubit blocks --- through electron shuttling, and on microsecond rather than millisecond timescales. They however travel along fabricated tracks rather than free space: permutations an atom array obtains by moving tweezers must here become collision-free motions on a physical lattice. We here present the first code and spin-qubit hardware co-design. We build an architecture whose geometry mimics that of a family of non-abelian groups, broad enough to host codes of excellent parameters: a hierarchy of nested conveyor-belt loops on a plain square lattice of shuttling tracks, in which every group multiplication becomes a rigid, globally controlled motion of whole qubit trains. We call it NeST, for Nested Shuttling Tracks. A code search over the family returns rate-20% mitten codes up to $[[1400,280,\leq 28]]$, and circuit-level simulations including shuttling dephasing give thresholds above $10^{-3}$ with sub-$50μ$s stabiliser cycles, two to three orders of magnitude faster than neutral-atom implementations. Via extrapolations, we estimate that this largest code may reach a logical error probability per qubit per round of $10^{-14}$, assuming a ten-fold improvement on early shuttling demonstrations, with other physical errors at p=0.1%. Logic is compatible with NeST too: for the [[150,30,10]] code we build a code-surgery gadget in which every qubit again moves only by rigid belt motions, at no qubit cost and a 29% increase in gate layers. This demonstrates that ultra-low-overhead fault tolerance and a fast clock speed are not competing goals, and that silicon spin qubits can supply both.

items.title_en: Symmetry-Guided Machine Learning of Spin-Dependent Nonlinear Hall Response
items.title_zh: 对称性引导的机器学习用于自旋相关非线性霍尔响应
items.abstract_en: A Berry-curvature dipole can produce a nonlinear Hall current even when the linear Hall response vanishes, but symmetry alone does not determine its magnitude or magnetic tunability. The interplay of structural symmetry, moment orientation, and carrier occupation is examined in a honeycomb model. Curvature maps and the band-summed dipole integrand reveal how velocity and the occupation window near the Fermi level select signed contributions. Removing threefold rotation permits a nonmagnetic dipole perpendicular to the surviving mirror. Generic magnetic reorientation activates the second component and tunes both components through positive and negative values. Global reversal preserves the dipole while reversing the intrinsic linear Hall conductivity, allowing a finite bulk dipole contribution from equally populated reversed domains under uniform-field averaging.A symmetry-constrained polynomial model predicts both dipole components for 256 held-out spin configurations, achieving coefficients of determination $R^2 > 0.9995$ at the reference chemical potential. At fixed carrier density, orientation-dependent shifts of the chemical potential modify the response and yield slightly larger prediction errors for the chosen model. Across the chemical-potential sweep,the prediction accuracy decreases more strongly for $D_y$,revealing an energy dependence of the surrogate's performance. Within semiclassical transport with a constant relaxation time, the calculated dipole determines the angular dependence of the quadratic current and its rectified and second-harmonic components. These results provide a quantitative representation of magnetic-orientation-dependent Berry-curvature dipoles and show how carrier occupation influences both the response and its predictability.

items.title_en: Efficient Ground-State Manifold Amplification for Rydberg Atom Arrays via Houdayer Cluster Updates
items.title_zh: 通过Houdayer簇更新实现里德堡原子阵列基态流形的高效放大
items.abstract_en: We demonstrate a hybrid quantum-classical approach for exploring ground-state manifolds of maximum independent set problems, in which quantum hardware supplies the initial solutions and an entirely classical post-processing algorithm expands them, increasing the solution diversity of quantum hardware measurements by up to several orders of magnitude. Quantum optimization devices, while capable of generating high-quality solutions, can suffer from fundamental sampling limitations. This is particularly problematic for applications that strongly depend on a large variety of uncorrelated optimal solutions. We apply the Houdayer cluster update algorithm to systematically expand quantum-generated solution sets through classical post-processing. We validate our approach on a test bed of 43 problem instances from QuEra's Aquila analog annealing device, achieving diversity amplification factors, defined as the increase in the number of distinct solutions at a given set size, of up to 11923x with a median of 24.3x across different problem scales and hardness parameters. Because exact ground-state degeneracies are known for these instances, the recovered fraction of the manifold can be measured rather than bounded: post-processing recovers a median of 21% of the ground-state manifold, and provably all of it for six instances. We also demonstrate that, in some cases, the classical post-processing can discover independent sets larger than those found by the quantum hardware, thus improving on solution quality and not just diversity. While the method is non-ergodic and cannot guarantee complete manifold coverage, it consistently discovers a larger number of high-quality, and in some cases strictly better, configurations than quantum sampling alone. This work demonstrates how simple classical post-processing can enhance the utility of quantum optimization results.

items.title_en: Photonic band structure by direct second-kind free-space boundary integral equations
items.title_zh: 基于直接第二类自由空间边界积分方程的光子能带结构
items.abstract_en: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via Müller's formulation. The wall equations, in turn, come from a stack formulation, in which Green's formula is applied on stacks of three cells, so that the wall self-interactions and the interactions between arcs sharing endpoints cancel exactly. The resulting system is of the second kind, Fredholm of index zero, and free of corner singularities, and the walls may be curved to keep the cell boundary away from the inclusions. Its operators are assembled once per frequency and reused for all Bloch vectors. We prove that every Bloch mode yields a nonzero null vector, and that a null vector comes from a Bloch mode exactly when its cell representation vanishes outside the cell, which gives an inexpensive test for spurious null vectors. The band frequencies are computed with a high-order Nyström discretization and the search of Bruno, Santana and Trefethen, which locates them as poles of adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) rational approximants to a randomly scalarized resolvent sampled on the real frequency axis. Numerical examples validate the method against exact and published band structures and include a challenging triangular lattice of air pores in a dielectric, whose cell requires curved walls.

items.title_en: A Solar Optical Clock
items.title_zh: 一种太阳光学钟
items.abstract_en: Precision spectroscopy underpins quantum sensing, atomic timekeeping, and the search for terrestrial-mass exoplanets. Finding an Earth-Sun analog requires fractional splitting of spectral features that rivals the precision of the best laboratory spectroscopy. This corresponds to resolution of a few parts in $10^5$ of a typical stellar spectral line, or a Doppler velocity precision of less than 10 cm s$^{-1}$. Only a few astrophysical spectrometers reach this regime, and only by dispersing starlight with large gratings and averaging thousands of lines. Here, we show that comparable precision can be achieved on a single solar line by leveraging techniques used in quantum sensors and optical clocks. A laser is frequency-locked to the 1565 nm solar Fe I line by coupling to a single mode of the solar thermal field and counted against an optical frequency comb referenced to the SI second, thus creating a solar optical clock. Operating at the fundamental photon-noise limit of thermal heterodyne spectroscopy, we achieve centroid precision of one part in $10^9$ of the optical frequency, or 30 cm s$^{-1}$ in radial velocity. We recover the Sun's five-minute acoustic oscillations and the expected Rossiter-McLaughlin signal during a solar eclipse. Combining these techniques from quantum sensing with a thirty-meter-class telescope could enable our demonstrated precision on the nearest Sun-like stars in a few hours. Multiplexing such absolute frequency measurements across lines with different magnetic sensitivity and formation depth would reduce averaging time and help disentangle stellar granulation and activity from the Doppler signature of terrestrial exoplanets, providing new approaches to address some of the most demanding measurements in astrophysical spectroscopy.

items.title_en: Tuning between collective dynamics and scrambling through initial-state symmetry alignment in long-range spin models
items.title_zh: 通过长程自旋模型中初始态对称性对准在集体动力学与扰乱之间进行调控
items.abstract_en: Long-range interactions in many-body quantum systems give rise to a wide range of dynamical phenomena, from collective dynamics well described by integrable mean-field models with symmetric all-to-all couplings, to fast scrambling of quantum information from disordered long-range interactions. Here, we investigate scenarios in which both regimes emerge within a single deterministic, translation-invariant XY spin model with long-range couplings. We consider a sparse powers-of-two (PWR2) graph, where each spin interacts with a logarithmic number of neighbors, and a power-law-decaying model. By altering the initial state via local perturbations on a completely symmetric state, we show that the dynamics changes from collective to scrambling as witnessed by bipartite and multipartite entanglement measures. We characterize this collective-to-scrambling crossover using Lyapunov exponents in the semiclassical regime, and show that the spectral properties of the coupling graph adjacency matrix provide a very efficient tool to predict the onset of fast scrambling. Our results offer a unified framework for controlling the switch between collective and scrambling dynamics in a setup accessible in experiments with neutral atoms in cavities or in tweezer arrays.

items.title_en: Quantum Simulation of the Static Yukawa Model via Effective Particles on a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulator
items.title_zh: 在囚禁离子量子模拟器上通过有效粒子对静态汤川模型进行量子模拟
items.abstract_en: Trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and circuit QED quantum computers naturally enable coupled qubit-boson simulations. Boson-fermion interactions arise in quantum field theory, where renormalization is required to obtain finite results. We study one of the simplest examples of a coupled fermion-boson system, the static Yukawa model, on the QSCOUT trapped-ion system. We use similarity renormalization to express the same physics in terms of effective particles described by different values of the renormalization parameter $s$. This enables us to map data taken in the window of bosonic occupancy that is experimentally accessible to larger occupancies of distinct effective particles. We use this to study strongly coupled, high-occupancy regimes despite limited readout ranges. Using a trapped-ion qubit-boson device on Sandia National Laboratories' QSCOUT platform, we demonstrate the time evolution of the static Yukawa model.

items.title_en: Chaos and scrambling in anisotropic Dicke and Rabi models
items.title_zh: 各向异性Dicke模型与Rabi模型中的混沌与扰乱
items.abstract_en: Identifying the quantum signatures of classical chaos remains a central question in quantum physics, and quantum scrambling provides a new perspective on this correspondence. We study two distinct limits of the same model to examine how the correspondence between chaos and scrambling changes across different regimes. The thermodynamic-limit anisotropic Dicke model exhibits a close correspondence between chaos and scrambling, whereas this correspondence breaks down in the large-frequency-ratio limit of the anisotropic Rabi model (ARM). The contrasting chaotic behavior in the two limits originates from the different numbers of classical degrees of freedom, whereas their similar scrambling behavior stems from eigenstate delocalization. This implies that, in the large-frequency-ratio limit, eigenstate delocalization alone is insufficient to qualify the ARM as a classically chaotic model. This finding suggests that identifying chaos in quantum systems requires jointly considering the classical degrees of freedom and eigenstate delocalization.

items.title_en: Scrambling Separates Superradiance from Quantum Chaos
items.title_zh: 扰乱将超辐射与量子混沌区分开来
items.abstract_en: Early studies on the Dicke model linked superradiance to quantum chaos, whereas later anisotropic Dicke and Rabi studies reached apparently conflicting conclusions. We resolve this tension by distinguishing global chaos from local instability. Along the isotropic Dicke path, a sweep at fixed low excitation energy crosses both the superradiant boundary and a nearby chaotic window, explaining the reported correlation. However, the anisotropic Dicke model can be chaotic in the normal phase and regular in the superradiant phase, making superradiance neither necessary nor sufficient for global chaos. A fidelity out-of-time-order correlator (FOTOC), in contrast, probes the local stability of the stationary point selected by the initial wave packet. The superradiant transition destabilizes the origin, whereas a change in anisotropy can restore its stability and create displaced saddles. Wave packets centered at these saddles exhibit exponential FOTOC growth even on a classically regular Dicke energy shell with Poisson statistics. This local sensitivity also enables quantitative spectroscopy: combined with the topology of stationary points and local density of states relations, FOTOC dynamics reconstructs the absolute amplitudes of spectral singularities in both models without fitting the density of states.

items.title_en: Mechanically reconfigurable layered GRIN lenses for mid-infrared
items.title_zh: 用于中红外的机械可重构分层GRIN透镜
items.abstract_en: This paper presents a concept of mechanically adjustable planar Gradientindex (GRIN) lens that can be used to realize reconfigurable focusing at mid-infrared (mid-IR) or millimeter-wave (mm-wave) frequencies. The concept is based on a multilayer design rooted in effective medium theory, where spatial refractive index profiles are synthesized using first-kind Chebyshev polynomials. Symmetric lateral displacement of the layers enables continuous modulation of the effective refractive index distribution, allowing controlled transitions between divergent, afocal, and convergent wavefronts. Numerical simulations demonstrate accurate focal tuning at mid-IR and mm-waves. In the mid-IR regime, focal lengths of about 56 μm and 24 μm are achieved with relative errors of around 4.4% and 10%, respectively. In the mm-wave regime, the lens produces focal lengths of about 158 mm and 128 mm with improved accuracies of 2.3% and 6.0%, respectively. The reconstructed refractive index profiles exhibit high similarity to ideal convex lens distributions, confirming the validity of the proposed synthesis approach. The proposed GRIN lens concept offers a scalable and physically interpretable approach to reconfigurable focusing, with potential applications in multimodal imaging, adaptive sensing, and telecommunication systems.

items.title_en: Orbital-angular-momentum control of localized Floquet states and photocurrents in Weyl semimetals
items.title_zh: 外尔半金属中局域Floquet态与光电流的轨道角动量调控
items.abstract_en: Structured light provides a route to controlling quantum materials not only through its polarization, but also through its spatial profile and orbital angular momentum (OAM). We develop real space theories of a Weyl semimetal driven by a vortex beam and show that optical OAM generates highly localized Floquet vortex states with pronounced circulating photocurrents. Exploiting cylindrical symmetry, we derive a Bogoliubov-de Gennes-like radial equation that resolves the states by angular momentum and reveals their evolution between the light-dressed Weyl cones. For Laguerre-Gaussian beams, the spatially varying drive produces strong hybridization between localized vortex states and bulk states. We complement this continuum description with a Wilson-lattice formulation that retains the full two-dimensional spatial structure and enables direct calculation of local photocurrents. Both approaches consistently identify OAM-induced vortex states localized around the beam axis. The lattice calculation further shows that these states support substantially stronger circulating current densities than the more extended surface states, with the largest current densities associated with the most strongly localized, low-angular-momentum vortex modes. Our results establish optical OAM as a tunable control parameter for creating and manipulating localized current-carrying states in Weyl systems and provide a real-space framework for studying photocurrents generated by spatially structured light.

items.title_en: Continuously Tunable Mid-Infrared Metalens Integrating Moiré and Pancharatnam-Berry Phases
items.title_zh: 集成莫尔相位与Pancharatnam-Berry相位的连续可调中红外超构透镜
items.abstract_en: A varifocal mid-infrared metalens designed for focusing applications is proposed to integrate both Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) and Moiré pattern-based mechanisms for rotational wavefront control. The metalens employs two identical nanostructured discs featuring germanium (Ge) meta-atoms on calcium fluoride (CaF2) substrates, operating as birefringent half-wave retarders with 99.95% Polarization Conversion Ratio (PCR) and 83.65% total transmission power at 2 μm wavelength. Full-wave numerical simulations demonstrate continuous focal length tunability from 45 μm to 12 μm by rotating the second disk from 30 deg. to 120 deg., corresponding to the numerical aperture values ranging from 22.99% to 68.67%. The proposed metalens maintains reconfigurable focusing regardless of the incident light polarization, while concurrently enabling polarization-controlled operation via a phase-modulation mechanism that yields inverse responses under Right Circular Polarization (RCP) and Left Circular Polarization (LCP) illuminations.

items.title_en: Stable charged energy and phase transitions in an anisotropic Dicke quantum battery with Kerr nonlinearity
items.abstract_en: Phase transitions (PTs) in quantum many-body systems offer a powerful route to manipulate the performance of quantum batteries (QBs). Here, we investigate an anisotropic Dicke QB with Kerr nonlinearity, focusing on the role of PTs in the charging process of the QB system. By analyzing how the Kerr nonlinearity reshapes the cavity level-spacing structure, we find that multiple near-degeneracies emerge at specific nonlinearity strengths. Away from the region of multiple near-degeneracies, the stable stored energy is governed primarily by the ergodic-nonergodic transition (ENET), whereas within this region it is controlled by first- and second-order dissipative phase transitions (DPTs). We employ Liouvillian spectral theory to quantify the critical slowing down associated with the DPTs, and use the Wigner function to characterize the properties of the cavity field in the vicinity of criticality. We optimize the charging process via reinforcement learning (RL) and reveal the physical mechanism underlying performance enhancement from the perspective of ergodic and nonergodic phase dynamics. Our results offer a feasible pathway for manipulating and optimizing quantum battery performance based on intrinsic PT behaviors.

items.title_en: Hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over finite chain rings
items.abstract_en: We give a bounded-error quantum polynomial-time algorithm for finding hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ over any effectively presented finite chain ring $R$. We call auxiliary group elements or subgroups used to extract information through oracle queries \emph{probes}. For chain length at least two, elementary abelian socle probes first recover the complete flag modulo the maximal ideal. When the residue field has size $q\ge3$, we reconstruct the flag recursively, lifting rank-one terminal members one digit at a time. The intermediate digits reduce to abelian hidden subgroup problems, while the final digit is a finite-field multiple-shift problem solved using learning from subset and Fourier sampling. For $q=2$, where distinct flags can have the same stabilizer, we instead lift the conjugate parabolic subgroup through the congruence filtration. A final linear system determines it modulo normalizer directions. The algorithm outputs generators with probability at least $1-ε$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\log|R|,\log(1/ε))$. Consequences include $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})$ for every $N\ge2$ and, with an explicit maximal-order presentation, $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal{O_K}/N\mathcal{O_K})$ for number fields $K$.

items.title_en: TexFlow: learning crystallographic texture on SO(3) manifold via normalizing flows
items.title_zh: TexFlow：通过归一化流在SO(3)流形上学习晶体学织构
items.abstract_en: Crystallographic texture is an important microstructural feature that statistically describes the orientations of grains in polycrystalline materials. Conventional texture analysis relies on the orientation distribution functions and pole figures, which are essential for interpreting the texture of a given material specimen but do not, by themselves, provide a direct framework for predictive modeling of process-structure-property linkages. Data- and machine learning-based approaches offer a means to address this gap; however, a key challenge lies in developing representations and learning frameworks that account for the manifold structure of rotations. In particular, many existing machine learning techniques are designed for Euclidean data and therefore are not readily applicable to rotations in the non-Euclidean group $\text{SO}(3)$. Here we introduce TexFlow, a conditional normalizing flow framework for texture modeling that learns a probability distribution over rotations in $\text{SO}(3)$ by construction. Rotations are encoded in a six-dimensional Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization representation which is then mapped back to valid rotations $\mathbf{R}\in\text{SO}(3)$. The framework supports conditional probabilistic modeling of texture $p(\mathbf{R}|c)$, where $c$ may represent processing parameters like temperature or deformation state. To complement conventional texture-analysis visualizations, such as pole figures and sections of the orientation distribution function, we further introduce Hopf-fibration visualizations as a compact global representation of texture. TexFlow is validated on both unconditional and conditional experimental and simulated texture datasets spanning diverse material systems. We show that TexFlow can accurately capture multimodal textures and their conditional evolution, providing a data-driven framework for establishing process-texture linkages.

items.title_en: Capturing Open Quantum System Dynamics with Compact Dressed Hamiltonians
items.abstract_en: We advance the compact dressed Hamiltonian (CDH) framework to simulate the dynamics of open quantum systems strongly coupled to structured bosonic environments. The CDH approach combines reaction-coordinate mapping with a polaron transformation, incorporating strong system-environment hybridization into a dressed representation before truncating the collective bosonic mode. As a result of this truncation, dynamical features are captured with substantially fewer states than in the original representation. The residual environment is treated using a weak-coupling Markovian quantum master equation. We benchmark the method for spin-boson-type models including a single spin, coupled spins, and spin ensembles, considering both resonant and off-resonant regimes and weak to strong system-bath coupling. Comparisons with hierarchical equations of motion and converged reaction-coordinate calculations demonstrate that the CDH representation systematically approaches the reference dynamics with a compact Hilbert space, accurately reproducing oscillation frequencies, relaxation behavior, and long-time populations over a broad parameter regime. The method further captures cooperative phenomena, including bath-mediated interactions, synchronization between spins, and signatures for collective emission. Beyond efficient time propagation, the CDH framework provides direct access to the spectrum and eigenmodes of the Liouvillian. We demonstrate that slow dynamical modes converge rapidly in the CDH representation, enabling identification of relaxation timescales without fitting time-dependent observables. As a whole, the CDH framework provides an efficient and physical description of strongly coupled open quantum-system dynamics.

items.title_en: CO$Φ$ - COmpiling PHotonics into dIgital quantum circuits
items.title_zh: CO$Φ$：将光子学编译为数字量子电路
items.abstract_en: Photonic and qubit-based (digital) approaches to quantum computing are largely regarded as separate paradigms. This article aims to bridge these paradigms by developing a method for mapping quantum-optical systems onto qubit-based quantum circuits. The key ingredient enabling this mapping is the introduction of a truncation of the Fock space describing single-mode optical states. Within this framework, representations of basic photonic operations are developed, including the phase-rotation operator, the displacement operator, the squeezing operator, and the beam splitter. Explicit quantum circuit constructions are provided for Fock-space truncations of dimension $N=2$ and $N=4$. We discuss benchmarking of the implemented operations and identify the regime of applicability and the limitations of the proposed method. The presented results can be used to simulate quantum optical circuits on qubit-based quantum computers, with special relevance to Gaussian Boson Sampling in the low-photon-number regime. To demonstrate the practical applicability of this approach, we complement the theoretical framework with a Python-based quantum programming tool CO$Φ$ that compiles Blackbird quantum-optics programs into qubit-based OpenQASM circuits using a truncated Fock-space encoding. The compiler is available on GitHub at https://github.com/Quantum-Cosmos-Lab/cophi.

items.title_en: Quantum Broker: QoS-Aware Distribution of Quantum Computations
items.abstract_en: Cloud-accessible quantum computing has made heterogeneous Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) available through provider platforms that differ in qubit technology, calibration state, queueing behavior, and pricing model. This heterogeneity makes execution management a quantum-engineering concern: a quantum circuit may be executable on several backends, but the resulting cost, latency, fidelity, and reproducibility depend on backend selection and on how measurement shots are allocated. This paper presents the Quantum Broker, an open-source and provider-agnostic framework for Quality-of-Service-aware quantum execution management. The framework operationalizes shot-wise distribution by exploiting the statistical independence of quantum measurement shots to dispatch a single circuit across multiple heterogeneous QPUs according to user-defined constraints and optimization objectives. It combines a modular execution architecture, interchangeable backend-profiling strategies, and the Quantum QoS Specification Language (QQSpec), a declarative language for expressing QoS requirements. Dispatch planning is supported by two solver backends: a mixed-integer linear-programming (MILP) solver, and a nonlinear dual-annealing solver. Experiments on benchmark quantum circuits and noisy simulator backends show that the Quantum Broker can produce feasible QoS-aware dispatch plans under heterogeneous backend conditions and can improve QoS satisfaction with respect to single-backend and naive multi-backend baselines. The results also expose a practical trade-off between planning time and dispatch quality, with the nonlinear solver producing higher-quality allocations at increased computational cost. Overall, the Quantum Broker provides an extensible execution-management layer for engineering portable, reproducible, and QoS-aware quantum software over fragmented quantum cloud infrastructures.

items.title_en: Floquet ground state order
items.abstract_en: Clean, interacting, periodically driven systems are believed to thermalize to featureless, infinite-temperature states that preclude the formation of stable ordered states. Here, we show stable quantum order, distinct from prethermal order, and its phase transitions in the ground state of the average-energy operator. Decomposing the time evolution into geometric and average-energy dynamics, we apply Geometric Floquet theory to identify the Floquet ground state. We derive a general variational principle to compute the Floquet ground state in large interacting periodically driven systems, and use it to develop a matrix product state algorithm. In driven nonintegrable chains of more than 100 interacting spins, our numerical simulations exhibit a gapped, area-law entangled Floquet ground state in extended parameter regimes; the ground-state manifold can support both dressed equilibrium order (e.g., Floquet antiferromagnets) and inherently nonequilibrium order (e.g., ground-state time crystals). This quantum order is protected by a finite average-energy gap, which closes at phase transition points upon changing model parameters. We decompose Floquet phases of matter into their equilibrium and nonequilibrium elements: whereas the Floquet ground state at any fixed time is a representative of an equilibrium phase of matter, the nonequilibrium content is entirely produced by the drive holonomy and is geometric. Finally, we identify quasilocal counterdiabatic driving as a mechanism for the stability against heating of gapped Floquet ground states in nonintegrable quantum systems, and argue why Floquet ground states evade the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis. Our work enables the study of interacting nonequilibrium matter deep into the many-body regime, and lays the foundations for the engineering of strongly correlated ordered quantum states.

items.title_en: Spin-wave circulation in unbounded ferromagnetic film
items.title_zh: 无界铁磁薄膜中的自旋波环流
items.abstract_en: A key challenge in spin-wave computing is steering spin waves through circuits without wave distortion or reflections. This often results in 1D propagation scenarios, which hinder applicability in 2D magnonic circuits. We demonstrate experimentally a novel approach using a hard magnetic spherical microparticle to guide spin-waves onto a closed path in a plain thin YIG film. The particle stray field induces a radially symmetrical magnetization landscape, which allows spin-waves to loop around. In parallel, we conducted micromagnetic simulations reproducing the experimental conditions, which confirm the circulation of spin-waves over several loops around the particle. This work demonstrates the possibility to steer spin-waves onto a circular path using inhomogeneous magnetic landscape, as well as advancing scalable spin-wave-based information processing technologies.

items.title_en: Ensemble basis-free coherence for quantum communication
items.abstract_en: The resource theory of coherence quantifies the quantum properties of states and their role in quantum information processing. Extending coherence theory to ensembles, the natural objects in quantum communication, remains an active research direction, with their operational potential still being explored. In this work, we establish a maximally coherent ensemble in every finite dimension: the continuous ensemble of pure states distributed according to the normalized Haar measure attains the tight upper bound on basis-free relative entropy ensemble coherence. We then prove that ensemble coherence bounds the effective informational advantage of postselective measurements over the Holevo quantity for two equiprobable pure states. Finally, for the qubit B92 QKD protocol, we show that the coherence of Alice's ensemble upper-bounds the secret key rate in the asymptotic regime. These results give ensemble coherence a quantitative operational meaning in quantum communication and cryptography

items.title_en: Steady-state cooperative emission of interlayer excitons in atomically thin light-emitting diodes
items.title_zh: 原子级薄发光二极管中层间激子的稳态协同发射
items.abstract_en: When an ensemble of emitters is confined within an optical wavelength, its radiation can become correlated, leading to cooperative emission. In two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) electron-hole bilayers, strong light-matter coupling enables the formation of interlayer excitons (IXs), long-lived dipolar excitations that provide an ideal setting for emergent collective phenomena. Here, we engineer an atomically thin light-emitting diode (LED) that generates electroluminescence (EL) from electrically injected IXs that are confined near the sample edges by an edge-enhanced fringing electric field. By measuring Hanbury-Brown-Twiss photon-photon correlations, we find pronounced signatures of collective decay in the form of large photon bunching followed by finite delay antibunching and bunching revivals. These emitter correlation signatures disappear when free charge carriers are doped to form a degenerate Fermi sea but are enhanced by the introduction of localized electrons. The results are consistent with a many-body quantum master equation that models the steady-state superradiant photon statistics of incoherently injected IXs. Our work establishes steady-state cooperative emission in a 2D TMD LED as a platform for studying strong light-matter interactions in electrically driven, non-equilibrium phases of Bose-Fermi mixtures.

items.title_en: Dynamics of two bosons with density-assisted tunnelling in a one-dimensional tilted lattice
items.abstract_en: We investigate the dynamics of two bosons in a tilted one-dimensional optical lattice with both standard and density-assisted tunnelling. The relative sign of the two tunnelling processes strongly affects the Bloch dynamics, leading to distinct reinforcing and competing regimes. We examine how the tunnelling processes generate correlations and find that, in the absence of onsite interactions, the early-time entanglement growth follows the same scaling with the density-assisted tunnelling amplitude. Finite onsite interaction changes this picture by breaking the symmetry between the reinforcing and competing regimes and enhancing the correlation differently in two regimes. This shows how the interplay between the two tunnelling mechanisms can change dyanmics and entanglement in a controlled few-body setting. Particularly, at equal tunnelling amplitudes, the doublon and singlon sectors decouple completely for arbitrary onsite interaction, lattice tilting, and initial state.

items.title_en: Dual Transverse Vortex-Spin-Momentum Locking in Rotating-Wave Structured Light
items.abstract_en: We theoretically investigate the transverse Poynting momentum and transverse spin angular momentum in circularly polarized rotating-wave structured light, and reveal a pair of \emph{dual} transverse vortex-spin-momentum locking. The transverse Poynting momentum exhibits a $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetric locking structure, being controlled independently by either the polarization or vortex handedness, yet invariant under their simultaneous reversal. Meanwhile, the transverse spin angular momentum is independent of the polarization but endowed with a crucial vortex-dependence inheriting such vortex-dependence from the Poytning momentum via curl operation. This finding expands the understanding of transverse optical linear and angular momenta in structured light and opens a new paradigm for vortex-spin-controlled optical manipulation.

items.title_en: Observable-Level Framework for Finite-Key Security in Coherent-One-Way Quantum Key Distribution
items.abstract_en: Practical security analysis of Coherent-One-Way (COW) quantum key distribution requires optical-device modeling, finite experimental statistics, and security inference to be treated consistently without conflating assumptions. We present a modular observable-level simulation framework organized through the pipeline θ_phys -> p -> O -> S_j(O), in which physical source, channel, receiver, and detector parameters determine detector-resolved event probabilities, a finite-block layer applies an effective dead-time treatment and generates aggregate detector counts, and interchangeable security evaluators act on the same observable record. The framework is verified against analytical optical, virtual-state, and finite-key relations and evaluated against reported experimental COW-QKD operating points. The Kato finite-key calculation reproduces the refined experimentally reported secure-key rates most closely at intermediate distances, with deviations of -1.5% at 50 km and -10.3% at 75 km. Monitoring bright-port decoy counts agree within 0.9-2.4%, while remaining distance-dependent dark-port residual identifies the principal model-sensitive observable of the present physical description. Applying Kato and Azuma-Hoeffding concentration treatments to identical detector records isolates the effect of finite-key statistical inference and shows substantially tighter Kato phase-error bounds for rare-event monitoring records studied here. Holding the Kato evaluator fixed, joint optimization of coherent-state mean photon number mu and receiver splitting fraction t_B increases model-predicted secure-key rate by 7.4-20.2% relative to optimization of mu alone with t_B = 0.3. The framework therefore provides a common computational interface for experimental reproduction, controlled security-model comparison, model-based protocol optimization, and modular adversarial stress testing in COW-QKD.

items.title_en: Dynamical Mean-Field Theory for Real Materials using Variational Quantum Compressed Time Evolution on a Quantum Computer
items.title_zh: 基于量子计算机上变分量子压缩时间演化的真实材料动力学平均场理论
items.abstract_en: We design a hybrid quantum-classical computational workflow, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory, to investigate the electronic properties of CaCuO2, a parent structure of high-temperature cuprate superconductors. Our approach uses a quantum algorithm as an impurity solver that is based on variational quantum compressed time evolution to compute the time-dependent Greens function on an IBM Heron quantum device. Utilizing error mitigation techniques and a Lehmann representation fitting procedure, we extract the density of states from the signal in the accessible time regime. Despite the significant challenges rooted in the residual imprecision of currently accessible NISQ devices, we successfully resolve the characteristic features of the spectral function. However, we find that the required numerical accuracy for full DMFT self-consistency exceeds current hardware capabilities, indicating that practical real-material DMFT applications will necessitate post-NISQ hardware developments.

items.title_en: Structured light for addressable two-qubit gates in medium-sized ion crystals: modeling motional and dephasing errors
items.abstract_en: Geometric phase gates with addressed laser radiation are widely used in trapped-ion quantum computers to drive high-fidelity entangling gates on an arbitrary qubit pair of a larger ion chain. Such programmable connectivity exploits the collective phonons to mediate the desired interaction, while simultaneously achieving robustness to their thermal fluctuations by a careful calibration of the gate time with respect to the laser and vibrational-mode frequencies. Crosstalk errors can arise when the spectator qubits, which should ideally remain idle during the gate, are partially driven by the laser fields. The minimal crosstalk, which is set by the laser beam size on the spectator ions, can be achieved when the addressing beams propagate perpendicular to the ion chain. However, this results in exciting the radial phonons, and can complicate achieving high-fidelities as the ion chain grows due to the so-called spectral mode crowding. In this work, we present the theoretical description of a scheme recently implemented by Faorlin et $al.$. This scheme overcomes these complications by engineering addressable state-dependent forces along the ion-chain with laser beams that propagate perpendicular to it through the use of structured light gradients. In this way, one can excite the axial phonons and avoid the spectral mode crowding, while simultaneously minimizing the crosstalk. We present a detailed derivation of the entangling gate scheme, together with analytical closed-form expressions for the leading contribution to the gate error caused by thermal motional fluctuations and dephasing noise. Our results confirm that such fluctuations account for up to 93$\%$ of the error budget under the operating conditions of the gate implemented by Faorlin et $al.$. We identify target parameters to reduce the motional error from the reported $10^{-3}$ to the $10^{-5}$ level.

items.title_en: Variable-Resolution Scattering Reveals Ensemble Properties
items.title_zh: 可变分辨率散射揭示系综性质
items.abstract_en: SAXS/SANS determine the size and structure of particles and macromolecules in solution. However, the conventional low-angle determination of the radius of gyration, Rg, cannot separately resolve its scattering-weighted mean and the width of its distribution. Because the apparent Rg includes a contribution from ensemble variance, the distribution width is required even to recover the mean Rg. Here, we introduce TENOR-SAXS, a method for estimating the scattering-weighted width of an Rg distribution by applying two anisotropic digital smearings to a single 2D scattering image. Comparing the smeared images provides curvature information unavailable from the conventional radial profile. The resulting observables require no explicit model of the native instrumental point-spread function and show only weak sensitivity over the range of native resolutions typical of SAXS measurements examined here. Analytical expressions are derived in the low-angle and narrow-distribution limits for ensembles described by a known or independently constrained single-particle form factor. For verification, we simulated scattering by particles with several form factors and ensembles with different size distributions, all agree well with the analytical theory. To leading order, the principal observable depends on the scattering-weighted mean and variance rather than on the distribution's functional form or higher moments. For simulated data corresponding to feasible synchrotron exposure times for biological samples, the distribution width and, expressed as a fraction of its mean, was recovered with a typical discrepancy of ~0.1, while the scattering-weighted mean Rg was recovered with ~2% relative discrepancy. TENOR-SAXS thus provides a framework for estimating ensemble width from existing 2D scattering data without explicit instrumental desmearing and for correcting the variance contribution to the apparent radius

items.title_en: Parallel Teleportation via AME(5,2) States on IBM Quantum Hardware
items.abstract_en: The five-qubit Absolutely Maximally Entangled AME$(5,2)$ state, whose every pair of qubits is maximally mixed so that all its information lives in non-local correlations, could in principle serve as a single shared quantum networking resource for teleporting two unknown qubits in parallel (each via its own Bell measurement and Pauli correction). Nonetheless, its hardware implementations remain scarce despite its theoretical importance. Here, we demonstrate parallel teleportation based on a five-qubit absolutely maximally entangled state, AME$(5,2)$, on the superconducting processor ibm_pittsburgh. We construct three-qubit Clifford decoders that extract two Bell pairs using three logical two-qubit gates for each of 60 inequivalent sender-receiver assignments. Using parallelization and classical Pauli frame post-processing, we retain reference-receiver entanglement on both channels after three teleportation rounds. With XY4 dynamical decoupling and the lowest-cost decoder, the final entanglement fidelities are $0.704\pm0.028$ and $0.680\pm0.022$, where uncertainties are pointwise $99\%$ confidence-interval half-widths over eight trials. Their lower bounds exceed the separability threshold of $1/2$. The decoder with lower circuit depth generally retains higher mean fidelity, and XY4 generally improves on XX. These results establish a hardware demonstration of two-channel entanglement transmission through repeated AME-assisted teleportation and provide compact decoding circuits for reconfigurable multipartite communication.

items.title_en: Black Holes are about Quantum Information
items.abstract_en: We review and analyse quantum information-theoretic approaches to black hole evaporation that purport to bring us closer to a resolution of the black hole information paradox. Our focus is on the Page-time paradox and on the contribution of the Hayden-Preskill model to understanding information release under the assumption of unitary evaporation. In this model, the black hole is taken to be a finite-dimensional quantum system whose dynamics can be represented by a quantum circuit, and its information-processing and communication abilities are studied. We identify the assumptions underlying this modelling and highlight two key features, fast scrambling dynamics and entanglement as a resource, that underpin the information release in the model. We argue that this reasoning exemplifies a broader change in how information is used in black hole physics, in which quantum information theory now provides a useful operational modelling framework. This application avoids earlier philosophical objections insofar as it is not based on epistemic ignorance and does not regard information as a substance. This line of reasoning has become central to the debate and, as such, warrants greater attention from the philosophy of physics community.

items.title_en: Dimension-free marginal inequalities for pure three-party states
items.abstract_en: The quantum marginal problem, concerned with the compatibility of local and global properties of a multipartite quantum system, is arguably one of the fundamental questions in quantum theory. In this article we introduce a novel family of inequalities bounding the allowed local spectra of a pure tripartite state. The number of inequalities in this family grows with the dimension of the system. Most importantly, the inequalities hold for arbitrary dimensions. For equal local dimension at most 4, they generate the complete set of eigenvalue inequalities.

items.title_en: Enhancement of Li and Na Storage in Janus HfSSe Monolayers by Co-Induced Electron-Deficient Chalcogen Sites: A First-Principles Study
items.abstract_en: The growing demand for high-capacity, fast-charging, and durable rechargeable batteries has intensified the search for advanced electrode materials, with two-dimensional materials offering large surface-to-mass ratios and short ion-diffusion pathways. Here, pristine and Co-doped Janus HfSSe monolayers were investigated as anode materials for Li-ion and Na-ion batteries using first-principles density functional theory. Pristine HfSSe was found to be dynamically stable and exhibited a 0.85 eV band gap, while Co substitution shifted the Fermi level toward the valence-band region. Adsorption of the first Li or Na layer induced metallic behavior, thereby improving charge transport. Co doping strengthened alkali-metal binding, with the most favorable Li and Na adsorption energies changing from -2.6125 and -1.9800 eV to -3.7405 and -3.0529 eV, respectively. Co doping created electron-deficient sites that enhanced Li/Na binding. Co-doped HfSSe accommodated up to four Li layers and three Na layers, increasing the theoretical capacities from 555.43 to 776.19 mAh/g for Li and from 370.29 to 582.14 mAh/g for Na. The average open-circuit voltages were 0.62 V for Li and 0.29-0.30 V for Na, with minimum migration barriers of 0.2153 and 0.1044 eV, respectively. These results identified Co-doped Janus HfSSe as a promising anode material for Li-ion and Na-ion batteries.

items.title_en: Polarization signatures of mixed scalar - pseudoscalar ALP - photon couplings in intense laser pulses
items.abstract_en: We investigate photon-to-axion-like-particle (ALP) conversion in a finite, linearly polarized laser pulse for a single ALP field with simultaneous scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type couplings to photons. Varying the collision angle between the strong pulse and the probe provides a continuous kinematic scan of the resonant ALP mass. For fixed kinematics in this setting, the scalar-type and pseudoscalar-type ALP conversion amplitudes interfere coherently, making both the photon-to-ALP conversion probability and the polarization rotation depend on the difference between the probe polarization angle $α$ and the coupling angle $θ_g$. Conversion is maximal at $|α-θ_g|=90^\circ$, where the polarization rotation vanishes, while the rotation magnitude peaks at $α-θ_g=45^\circ$ modulo $90^\circ$, where conversion is half-maximal.
